name: Pueblo of Acoma grant, confirmed by Congress December 22, 1858 (Royce Area 663)
citation: Act of December 22, 1858, ch. 5, 11 Stat. 374 (confirmation); patent November 19, 1877
promises: Congress confirmed the Pueblo of Acoma's land claim, as reported favorably by the Surveyor General of New Mexico, and ordered it surveyed and patented (Act of December 22, 1858, 11 Stat. 374).
The Act says the confirmation is only a relinquishment of the United States' own title and claim, and does not affect any adverse valid rights.
Royce records the grant as 95,792 acres, a Spanish grant of 1689 (Royce gives no patent date; the Indian Claims Commission gives a patent of November 19, 1877 for 95,791.66 acres).
landTaken: None found for the grant. The Commission found that a 283.24-acre conflict between the Cubero grant and the Acoma grant did not affect Acoma's title, because the Court of Private Land Claims excluded land the United States had already patented.
compensation: Acoma is not named in the Act of May 31, 1933.
today: Acoma's claim for its aboriginal land outside the grant went to the Indian Claims Commission (Docket 266), which held in 1967 that the United States extinguished Acoma's title to that land without compensation; it ended in a stipulated final judgment of $6,107,157 on June 17, 1970. That concerns other land and is not counted against this grant. The Pueblo Lands Board reported on October 5, 1929 that the Acoma grant and the 1928 reservation were Acoma's only lands.

openQuestions: The date 1886-10-01 in treaties.json is not an event date for this land. Royce prints the Pueblo grants under a block headed 'Oct. 1, Act of Congress, Stat. L. XI, 374'; 11 Stat. 374 is the Act of December 22, 1858, which confirmed the grant. This is land the Pueblo kept, not land it ceded. Not edited.
The Pueblo Lands Board in 1929 gave the Acoma grant as 94,169 acres, against 95,791.66 acres in the 1877 patent; the difference was not explained in what was read.
The Pueblo of Acoma's own account of its grant was not located (acomaskycity.org returned 403; puebloofacoma.org has no land history).
The $6,107,157 judgment was entered on a stipulation and is a settlement, so it is not recorded as a breach finding even for the aboriginal land.
The statute link in treaties.json (ops.libs.uga.edu) was not used; the Act was read on govinfo.
